newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures end mostly up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures end mostly up on short covering.

text.p: CME hog futures rebounded from recent sharp losses and prices ended mostly higher as short covering offset pressure from weak fundamentals, traders said.

Although futures looked technically weak going into the opening, support from forecasts for fewer hogs going into the end of the year prompted short covering and bolstered futures. October also firmed late after falling early on further long liqudation and unwinding of bull spreads, traders said.
Prices ended up 0.700 to off 0.100 cent a lb with December up most at 54.950 cents. Most months ended at day's highs.

"Cash has been under some pressure lately but I expect December to stabilize. Packers would like to break the market but there are not enough hogs to fill their slaughter capacity" going into the end of the year, said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates.
However, deferred contracts, second quarter and beyond, were seen showing continued resistance from expected increases in hog production, Harper said.
"With corn cheaper, I think there is a pretty good chance we are going to see a little bit of expansion hit the hog market numbers by next summer," he said.
